# Issue 85 executable probe fixture

This is a small probe contract and stateful Dart guest, not Tina's production plugin API. The positive component is ABI-stamped with one custom section named `tina.embedder-abi`, whose payload is little-endian `u32(1)`.

## Rebuild the real Dart component

Use an isolated `wasm.dart` checkout on the integrated generator source branch, the pinned Dart SDK `3.14.0-edge.e7112ac2438cd4f5ac0c832c27ce75bb10b02420`, an already-warmed private Cargo target, and an existing `runtime_helpers.wasm`. The helper is generated by `pkg/wasm_tools/tool/build_runtime_helpers.sh`, which uses nightly `-Zbuild-std`; this slice deliberately reuses a prebuilt helper instead of rebuilding it.

```sh
cd /tmp
ISSUE85_CARGO_TARGET=/path/to/private/warmed/target \
ISSUE85_RUNTIME_HELPERS=/path/to/existing/runtime_helpers.wasm \
  /path/to/wasm.dart/pkg/test_runner/testdata/plugin_probe/regenerate_fixture.sh \
  /path/to/isolated/wasm.dart-checkout /tmp/plugin.component.wasm
```

The script checks the SDK revision, refuses the precompiled-generator branch, rebases workspace package roots to the isolated checkout, uses the source `wasm_tools` hook, writes generated artifacts under its private `/tmp/issue85-plugin-probe.*` directory, reuses the supplied private Cargo target, keeps source-hook metadata in the isolated checkout, and removes its temporary `target` symlink and runtime-helper copy on exit. It does not promise byte-identical output because the SDK output includes fixture source paths from the unique temporary directory. `stamp_abi.py` appends and rechecks the exact ABI section.

`hook/link.dart` reads the generated plugin ABI JSON and supplies the component linker asset. The source hook is `pkg/wasm_tools/hook/build.dart`; this source checkout has no `lib/src/wit_gen/precompiled/`, so it builds the patched generator source. Published platform precompiled libraries remain a separate release task.

## Rebuild admission-negative components

After placing the regenerated positive component at `plugin.component.wasm`, run:

```sh
python3 tool/make_admission_fixtures.py "$PWD" /path/to/wasm-tools
```

The script prints the positive component to WAT, applies deterministic name/schema/ownership mutations or an unreachable start body, then parses and validates each resulting component. The checked-in negative fixtures cover interface/world revisions, an unsupported imported member, run/descriptor schema mismatch, borrow-versus-own mismatch, and import denial before guest initialization. There is not yet a distinct-resource-identity or wrong-member-kind binary fixture; the validator rejects those shapes, but this slice does not claim that adversarial test coverage.

The generator currently does not support direct `WorldItem::Type` imports (`import_types` is empty); the imported-resource cleanup scan handles imported interfaces. A separate regression proves an imported alias to a resource defined by an exported owner interface is treated as owner-local and receives no guest borrow-table drop.

## Tina prompt fixture

`plugin.component.wasm` uses `plugin_authoring_stateful.dart` for the original counter-broker tests. `tina_prompt_plugin.component.wasm` uses `tina_prompt_plugin.dart` for the real Tina bridge. It calls only `session.read-context` and returns the session/model JSON plus its Store-local run count.

To rebuild the Tina fixture, set `ISSUE85_PLUGIN_SOURCE` to the absolute path of `tina_prompt_plugin.dart` when running `regenerate_fixture.sh`. Leave it unset for the original fixture. Keep the existing private-target, pinned-SDK and runtime-helper inputs. Temporary source paths can change output hashes. The admission-negative fixtures derive from the original `plugin.component.wasm`.
